measurement: P2 — mechanism E (LoRA) against the baseline, on the form verifier
findings: THE RULED 3 EPOCHS OVERFITS 63 EXAMPLES, and three independent signals agree: val loss bottoms at iter 60 (1.388) and climbs to 1.590 by 189 while train loss falls 1.935 -> 0.179; 七絕 form pass HALVES from 32.0% to a 17.3% mean over three seeds; and Latin-token intrusion TRIPLES from ~27 of 200 to ~85.

THE ITER-60 CHECKPOINT (one epoch) IS NOT DESTRUCTIVE: 七絕 34.0% against the baseline's 32.0%, and Latin intrusion 16 of 200 — BELOW the baseline's 27. The val-loss minimum picked the right checkpoint.

The degradation is far larger than seed noise: the three 3-epoch seeds give 七絕 18/20/14 percent, a 6pp spread, against a 15pp gap to the baseline. Running three seeds is what makes that sentence sayable.
七律 remains the form not to score on: the baseline's own two seeds are 40% and 12%.

Mechanism E did NOT improve form at 3 epochs and did not clearly improve it at 1 epoch either. It is a voice intervention and the form verifier is not where its benefit, if any, should appear — but it CAN do harm there, and at 3 epochs it does.
bounds: The iter-60 arm is ONE SEED. Its 34.0% carries the same +/-6.6pp binomial SE as any other 50-sample rate here, and it should have two more seeds before anything rests on it.
The training split is form-imbalanced: 七律 41, 七絕 13, 五絕 4, 五律 1, unregulated 11, over 63 examples. The 絕 forms are the ones scored and the ones least trained.
The form verifier does not read Latin characters at all — the extractor strips to CJK — so intrusion is counted separately and is NOT part of any pass rate above.
Nothing here is the JUDGE. P2's actual question is discrimination, which is 理's harness on the held-out 33; this is the form half only.
One base, one rank, one learning rate, one LoRA run. No sweep.
